svg.title: Step 9 mockup 05: the LAN board
svg.text: 05 · The LAN board: the legacy LAN display, reborn as a built-in layout
Six boxes of data widgets and the alive chips in the header, landscape and portrait. Layouts are data: a theme restyles it, an organiser changes its boxes in Screen studio.
Use case: a café or lobby TV all evening, or the Main screen at night through a scene (U2, U3).
Portrait, 1080 × 1920: a TV on its side
The header's chips are the legacy alive chrome (D3): HOT when a game has 4 or more players, VOICE
when a room has 5 or more, SPIKE when 5 or more came online in 10 minutes. Thresholds are the legacy
defaults, per event (O7). A chip names the box it belongs to; no separate pulse strip (L6).
The six boxes: Right now, the day's graph, tonight's top games (player-hours), now playing, voice rooms
and the tournament's next heat. At most 4 rows a box, type as on Pulse (amendment 2).
A built-in layout like Pulse or Dashboard (theming's layouts as data), with a portrait twin; any zone may
pick it, and a scene may switch a zone to it for the night (U3).
Nothing here is crew-only: it shows what the hub shows a guest, minus the rotating check-in code (U1,
